calls.reason: OpenAI kept raising (a $122B round in March 2026) and burned about $8B in 2025, which fits the pattern so far. But no finite run of rounds can show a need to raise 'in perpetuity', which is the core of the claim.
The condition never happened: PYMNTS reported in May 2026 that OpenAI was operating and preparing an IPO. With OpenAI still in business, the predicted market collapse cannot be judged.

BBC reporting confirms Google's emissions rose 48% from 2019 to 2023 and links it to AI compute. But nothing in the packet measures AI's share of that rise or any 'massive' worldwide emissions effect.

OpenAI survived past two years. Altman's blog reports a roughly 150x fall in price per token, but that is a price, not a cost. Projected total compute spending is rising. The cost basis is unclear, so the necessity claim cannot be tested.
OpenAI announced $6.6B in new funding on October 2, 2024. That came after Microsoft's July 30 earnings call and well before the late-January 2025 deadline.

Large funds (SoftBank, Fidelity, MGX) joined a $6.6B round, and SoftBank later held about 11% after its $40B-round investment. That fits a huge round from big funds taking large stakes, though necessity is unproven.
